content:
{
  "findings": [
    {
      "title": "Inconsistent hemoglobin threshold for gastric cancer",
      "quote": "Hemoglobin ≥ 9 g/dL. NOTE: Patients requiring ongoing transfusions or growth factor support to maintain hemoglobin ≥9 g/dL are not eligible. (> 8 g/dL in Gastric Cancer / Gastroesophageal Cancer Indications)",
      "page": 43,
      "section": "Inclusion Criteria",
      "category": "consistency",
      "severity": "major",
      "explanation": "The hemoglobin threshold is stated as ≥9 g/dL but then a lower threshold of >8 g/dL is given for gastric/gastroesophageal cancer indications. This inconsistency may lead to confusion and potential enrollment of patients who do not meet the primary threshold.",
      "fix": "Clarify the exact hemoglobin threshold for each tumor type and ensure consistency throughout the protocol."
    },
    {
      "title": "Exclusion of HER2-overexpressing breast/gastric cancer may conflict with inclusion of HER2-mutant tumors",
      "quote": "HER2 overexpressing (IHC3+ or IHC2+/ISH+) adenocarcinoma of breast, gastric or gastroesophageal junction as determined by local HER2 testing.",
      "page": 47,
      "section": "Exclusion Criteria",
      "category": "consistency",
      "severity": "major",
      "explanation": "This exclusion criterion may inadvertently exclude patients with HER2-mutant tumors that also overexpress HER2, even though the inclusion criteria allow HER2 mutations regardless of expression. This could limit enrollment and create ambiguity.",
      "fix": "Specify that HER2 overexpression is only exclusionary if not associated with a qualifying HER2 mutation, or align with inclusion criteria."
    },
    {
      "title": "Exclusion of HER2 mutant NSCLC may be overly restrictive",
      "quote": "HER2 mutant NSCLC.",
      "page": 47,
      "section": "Exclusion Criteria",
      "category": "amendment_risk",
      "severity": "major",
      "explanation": "Excluding all HER2-mutant NSCLC patients seems overly broad, as the study aims to include HER2 mutations across tumor types. This may reduce enrollment and could be amended if evidence supports benefit in NSCLC.",
      "fix": "Consider including HER2-mutant NSCLC or provide a clear rationale for exclusion."
    },
    {
      "title": "QTcF threshold differs by sex but not by protocol standard",
      "quote": "Corrected QT interval by Fridericia's formula (QTcF) prolongation to > 470 msec (females) or > 450 msec (males) based on average of the screening triplicate 12-lead ECG.",
      "page": 47,
      "section": "Exclusion Criteria",
      "category": "advisory",
      "severity": "minor",
      "explanation": "The QTcF thresholds are sex-specific, which is standard, but the protocol does not mention how to handle patients on QT-prolonging medications or with electrolyte abnormalities, which could affect safety monitoring.",
      "fix": "Add guidance on managing concurrent QT-prolonging drugs and electrolyte monitoring."
    },
    {
      "title": "No explicit safety monitoring for ILD beyond baseline",
      "quote": "Has a history of (non-infectious) interstitial lung disease (ILD)/pneumonitis that required steroids, has current ILD/pneumonitis, or where suspected ILD/pneumonitis cannot be ruled out by imaging at screening.",
      "page": 47,
      "section": "Exclusion Criteria",
      "category": "completeness",
      "severity": "major",
      "explanation": "While ILD is an exclusion criterion, the protocol lacks a detailed plan for monitoring ILD during the study, which is critical for T-DXd given its known ILD risk. The endpoints mention AEs but not specific ILD monitoring.",
      "fix": "Include a specific ILD monitoring plan (e.g., regular imaging and symptom assessment) in the safety section."
    },
    {
      "title": "Primary endpoint ORR may not capture durable benefit",
      "quote": "Confirmed ORR according to RECIST v1.1, as assessed by ICR.",
      "page": 37,
      "section": "Objectives and Endpoints",
      "category": "advisory",
      "severity": "minor",
      "explanation": "ORR is a reasonable primary endpoint for a tumor-agnostic study, but it may not reflect durable responses. Including DoR as a key secondary endpoint is helpful, but consider a co-primary or sensitivity analysis for durable responses.",
      "fix": "Consider adding a secondary endpoint for durable response rate (e.g., responses lasting ≥6 months)."
    },
    {
      "title": "Washout period for antibody-based therapy may be too long",
      "quote": "Antibody-based anti-cancer therapy: ≥ 4 weeks.",
      "page": 43,
      "section": "Inclusion Criteria",
      "category": "burden",
      "severity": "minor",
      "explanation": "A 4-week washout for all antibody-based therapies may be unnecessarily long for some agents with shorter half-lives, potentially delaying treatment for patients who need it.",
      "fix": "Consider a washout based on 5 half-lives or a shorter fixed period for certain antibodies."
    },
    {
      "title": "Tumor sample requirement may be difficult to meet",
      "quote": "All patients must provide an existing FFPE tumor sample for retrospective central HER2 testing. The sample should be obtained at the time of diagnosis of metastatic or locally advanced unresectable disease.",
      "page": 43,
      "section": "Inclusion Criteria",
      "category": "amendment_risk",
      "severity": "major",
      "explanation": "Requiring a sample from the time of metastatic diagnosis may be challenging if such a sample is not available, and the protocol only allows a pre-enrolment sample if the metastatic sample is unavailable. This could lead to many screen failures.",
      "fix": "Allow any available tumor sample (primary or metastatic) if the metastatic sample is not available, and clarify acceptable alternatives."
    }
  ]
}
